verdict.rationale: Reader documents a dedicated `x-respond-timing` header for explicit control over when it returns, framed as a latency-versus-completeness trade-off. `x-wait-for-selector` adds element-level control over when the page is considered ready. missing for 10: documentation of the specific timing modes or values and their behavior, independent or hands-on corroboration that the timing control works as described.

support.subject: As a developer, I can trade off latency against completeness by controlling exactly when content is returned

citations.quote: `x-respond-timing` — explicit control over *when* Reader is willing to return. Trade off latency against completeness
